item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
This is an absolutely beautiful piece of literature. The imagery is stunning and presented with such remarkable clarity that I was wholly drawn into the bliss felt by the narrator. You artfully displayed a truly intimate moment, capturing the pure ecstasy of two lovers, bound together in the immortal embrace of copulation. It was passionate, raw, and fantastic.

The gross sexual conduct is easy to overlook precisely because it is not written as gross, sexual conduct. Metaphor upon metaphor can be lain over this and have it fit; any total and complete surrendering of the will. That being said, it still has the pornographic root, and even that is inordinately well-represented. There is a reason the "romance novels" are so popular, and this hits that style square on the head, even if many would find the characters a bit icky.

And as far as "icky" goes, you hit that even more square-esque.

DrClef, if this were to truly be your legacy, then kudos to you for leaving us with a masterpiece.

+1

I think that the disclaimer could maybe be less flippant, and more of a straight sexual content warning though. It seems somewhat at odds with the actual tone of the story, but maybe that is intentional?

The disclaimer's tone is the same as that of his author post, almost all of the comments (especially on the first page), and how he was talking about the prompt/how the prompt came up that night in 19 when he first said he'd write it. We'll never really know if this tale is tongue-in-cheek or not, and I'm starting to think that might've been Clef's intention from the beginning; after all, he posted it on April Fool's Day, and it formed from a jokey prompt in chat.

while this is just a very, very, very gross sex scene

+ edit: I guess I should collapse this for addressing NSFW topics
- hide

Indeed it is. It's sexual body horror. Or is it? When it comes to this particular tale, the interpretation depends on what the reader wants to see. Sure, it was posted on April 1st and Clef's joking in the author post, but who knows why people are upvoting it? It could be for the squick, it could be for the OTT-ness, hell, it could be because they're into guro. We really don't know, and we really can't judge. All we have is the text. That's what's so clever about it.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Cyan, we're buddies, but there is a reason I don't visit your tumblr except maybe in incognito mode and with the doors locked and windows shuttered, but don't tell anyone, ok?, and it's because I don't associate this site or its fiction with, like, anything arousing.

I'm not staff and doubt I could get a solid rallying behind these sentiments even if I were, so all that's left is my votes, and I see no merit behind this sort of fiction besides maybe shock horror. Other sorts of adult fiction (here meaning "erotica and crackfic") are also outside the range of what I want to see on the site. I understand that sex is a thing that people do, like, all the time, but "horny" is not really on the list of emotions I want to associate with this site. This is why I neutral-voted this, but downvoted this story, here: that scene actually served more purposes than just showing two people getting their freaky on, namely graphically depicting how some of the characters feel about each other, while this is just a very, very, very gross sex scene.
